transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose what finally pushed me to come in was that I lost my temper in a way that really surprised me. I was helping out with some of the younger volunteers, and there was this tablecloth that was crooked — just a tablecloth, nothing important really — and I snapped at one of them over it. Raised my voice, got sharp with him. That’s not how I usually speak to people, especially young folks who are just trying to help.

Afterward I kept thinking, why did I do that? It was such a small thing, and I made it into something bigger. It bothered me enough that I thought maybe I ought to talk to someone before I do it again.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or feelings that you feel compelled to repeat or act on?

I don’t think so, no… not in the way you’re saying, I don’t believe. I mean, I do go back over things in my head sometimes, probably more than I should — like what I said, whether I handled something badly — but I wouldn’t say I feel forced to repeat anything or do some particular action to make it stop.

I’m not washing my hands over and over or checking locks a dozen times, if that’s what you mean. It’s more just… I get bothered by something and then I think about it too much afterward. But compelled to act on it? No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Do you find yourself having thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yes… yes, I think that’s probably the thing that’s been bothering me most, if I’m being honest. It’s not like I sit down and decide to think about it. I’ll be doing something ordinary — sitting at my kitchen table, maybe trying to have my coffee or sort through the mail — and then out of nowhere I hear that man’s rough voice in my head again. Clear as anything, like he’s right there.

Or I’ll suddenly see that donation envelope hitting the ground. Just that moment, over and over, even when I’m trying to think about something else. It’s strange because nothing is happening in the room, it’s quiet, and still my mind just pulls me right back to it. I try to shake it off, tell myself to stop going over it, but it comes in anyway.
Do these repeating thoughts cause you a lot of distress?

Yes… they do. I mean, I don’t fall apart every time, but it upsets me more than I’d like to admit. It’s the way it comes out of nowhere. I can be sitting at my kitchen table, just minding my own business, and suddenly I hear that man’s rough voice again in my head, or I see that donation envelope hitting the ground like it’s happening right in front of me.

And it’s not even that I’m trying to remember it. That’s what bothers me. If I sat down and chose to think about it, maybe that would be one thing, but this just sort of pushes its way in. Then I feel tense and unsettled, and it takes me a while to get back to whatever I was doing. It makes a quiet moment not feel quiet anymore, if that makes sense.
Did something particularly stressful or traumatic happen to you before these repeating thoughts and loss of temper started?

Yes… yes, there was. It started after I was robbed outside the bank. That was about a week ago now, though it feels a little strange saying “only a week,” because it keeps replaying enough that it feels longer in my head.

Before that happened, I wasn’t having these repeating thoughts like this, and I wasn’t getting so worked up. But ever since then — since that incident outside the bank — it’s been going on. I keep thinking, well, maybe in another week it’ll fade, but right now it’s still very much there.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities since the robbery outside the bank?

Yes… I suppose I have been, though I didn’t quite think of it that way at first. I’ve been taking the long way around now so I don’t have to pass the bank. It’s silly, maybe, because it’s just a building, and I know that, but when I come near it I can feel myself wanting to steer away before I even really decide to.

And there’s the festival storage room, too. I haven’t gone in there since. There are things in there I probably should check on, but I keep putting it off because it brings the whole thing too close again. Just being around that sort of donation stuff… it makes me feel like I’m right back there, and I’d rather not put myself through it if I can avoid it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since the robbery?

Yes… I have. Not terribly in the sense that I’m up pacing all night, but it’s definitely changed since the robbery.

I’ll get into bed feeling tired — really tired, like my body wants to sleep — and then once the house is quiet, I just sort of lie there listening. Every little noise catches my attention. A creak, a car going by, something settling in the walls… I find myself straining to hear it, as if I’m waiting for something, though I know I’m at home and nothing is happening.

And then when I do sleep, it doesn’t feel very deep. I’ve been waking up before dawn, earlier than I need to, and I’ll just be lying there thinking, “Well, that’s it then, I suppose I’m awake.” It leaves me feeling like I hardly slept, even if technically I was in bed for hours.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're in a safe environment?

I’m not sure I’d say “constantly,” no. I mean, I understand what you’re asking, but I don’t know that I’m walking around all day scanning for danger exactly.

It’s more… I’m aware I don’t feel quite like myself, but if you mean am I always looking out the window or checking every corner or expecting someone to come at me, I don’t think I’ve noticed that in a clear way. Maybe I’d have to think about it more, because sometimes you don’t realize you’re doing something until someone points it out. But sitting here now, I can’t honestly say yes, that’s definitely happening.
Are there any specific reminders of the robbery, such as news reports or conversations about it, that you've been trying to avoid?

Yes, I have been avoiding certain reminders, though not so much the news reports specifically. It’s more the places and the things connected to it.

I’ve been taking the long way around so I don’t have to pass the bank. I tell myself it’s just more convenient or that I wanted a bit of a walk, but if I’m honest, it’s because going past there makes it feel too close again. Even seeing the front of the building out of the corner of my eye, I feel myself wanting to turn away.

And I still haven’t gone into the festival storage room. There are things in there I probably ought to look at, but I keep putting it off. It’s tied up with the whole thing in my mind now, and I don’t like how it brings me right back to it. So yes, I suppose I’ve been avoiding reminders, just maybe in a quieter way than refusing to watch the news or anything like that.
How long have you been experiencing these repeating thoughts and feelings of distress after the robbery?

It’s been about a week now, I’d say. Since the robbery outside the bank.

It started more or less right after that happened — not weeks before or anything like that. At first I thought maybe it was just the shock of it, you know, the first day or two being rattled, but it hasn’t quite lifted the way I expected. So… yes, about a week.
Would you say your avoidance of certain places or activities is interfering with your daily life or routine?

Yes… I think it is, more than I wanted to admit at first.

I usually help keep things moving for the Día de los Muertos event — you know, organizing, checking on what still needs doing, making sure people have what they need. It’s something I’ve done for a long time, and normally I’m pretty dependable with it. But lately I just haven’t been keeping up the way I usually do. I put things off, or I avoid going near certain parts of it, and then the day goes by and I realize I didn’t handle what I said I would.

And I’ve stopped going to card nights too. That’s not like me either. It’s not that I don’t care about the people there — I do. But right now I don’t feel steady around people, if that makes sense. I feel like I’d rather stay home than sit there trying to act normal. So yes, I’d say it’s starting to get in the way of my routine. Not in some dramatic way, maybe, but enough that I notice I’m not doing the things I normally do.
Would you say that avoiding these places or activities is something you feel like you have to do to cope with your feelings, or is it more of a preference?

It feels more like something I have to do, if I’m being honest. I wouldn’t call it a preference, exactly. It’s not like I enjoy taking the long way around or like I’ve decided, “Oh, I’d rather not go past the bank today.” It’s more that when I think about passing it, something in me just tightens up, and I start finding reasons not to.

I’ll tell myself the other route is fine, that it only adds a little time, that I needed the walk anyway… but underneath that, I know I’m doing it because I don’t want to see the bank. Even just being near it makes the whole thing feel too close again, like I’m right back at that feeling.

And the festival storage room is similar. I haven’t gone in there because it’s tied to all of it now in my head. I keep thinking I should just open the door and get on with what needs doing, but then I stop myself. So, no, I don’t think it’s just a preference. It feels like I’m avoiding those places because it’s the only way I can keep myself from getting stirred up.
Would you say that avoiding these places or activities is significantly impacting your ability to function in your daily life?

Yes… I’d say it is, though maybe not in a way where everything has fallen apart. I’m still getting through the day, but I’m not functioning like I normally do.

The clearest thing is the Día de los Muertos event. I usually help organize things, and people kind of count on me to keep track of what needs to be done. I’ve done that for years, so it bothers me that I haven’t been keeping up with it the way I usually would. I’ll mean to make a call, or check on something, or go handle something, and then I just… don’t. Or I put it off because it means being around certain places or people, and then I feel bad because someone else has to pick up the slack.

And I’ve stopped going to card nights too, which is a regular part of my week. That may sound small, but at my age those routines matter. It’s where I see people, talk, laugh a little, feel normal. Lately I don’t feel steady enough around people, like I’d have to pretend I’m fine the whole time, and I just don’t have it in me. So I stay home instead.

So yes, it’s affecting my daily life. Mildly maybe, compared to some people, but enough that I notice I’m pulling back from the things I normally do.
Would you say that avoiding these places or activities is something you feel like you're doing most of the time, or is it more occasional?

I’d say it’s more than occasional, yes. Not every single minute of the day, but it’s become sort of… built into how I’m moving around now.

Like with the bank, I’ve been taking the long way around so I don’t have to pass it. At first I told myself it was just once or twice, just because I didn’t feel up to it that day. But then I noticed I was doing it again, and again, almost without even deciding. I’ll be walking or driving and before I know it, I’ve already planned a route that keeps me away from there. It’s not like I sit down and make a big dramatic decision about it — it’s more automatic than that. I just don’t want to see it, don’t want to get that feeling in my chest, so I go around.

And with the festival storage room, I haven’t gone in there at all. I know there are probably things in there I should be checking on, and normally I would’ve just gone in, looked over the supplies, made a list, done what needed doing. But now even thinking about opening that door makes the whole thing feel too close again. So I keep putting it off.

So… I guess I’d say it’s happening most of the time when those places come up. It’s not that I’m avoiding everything in life, but those specific places, yes — I keep steering away from them.
Have your symptoms been present for more than a month?

No… no, it hasn’t been more than a month. It feels longer, honestly, because the days have been sort of dragging, but when I count it out, it’s only been about a week.

It started after the robbery outside the bank. Ever since then, that’s when all of this really began. So, no — not a month. More like a week, maybe a little over or under depending on how you count it, but about a week.
Have your symptoms been getting worse or staying about the same since they started?

I’m not completely sure how to judge that, to be honest. It hasn’t been that long, so part of me feels like I don’t have enough distance from it yet to say, “Oh, this is clearly worse,” or “this is clearly better.”

Some moments feel about the same as they did right after it started, and then other moments catch me off guard and feel heavier. But I don’t know if that means it’s actually getting worse, or if I’m just more tired from dealing with it day after day. You know, after a few days of being on edge and rearranging what I do, it sort of wears you down, so it can feel worse even if the actual problem hasn’t changed much.

If I had to put it simply, I’d say it’s mostly staying about the same… maybe with some ups and downs. I haven’t noticed a clear steady improvement, but I also don’t think I can honestly say it’s been sharply getting worse. It’s just still there, and I’m still having to work around it.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since the robbery?

Yes… I have noticed some changes. I wouldn’t say I’ve cut everybody off or anything like that, but I’m not showing up the way I usually do.

The biggest thing is the Día de los Muertos event. Normally I’m pretty involved with organizing it — making calls, checking what still needs to be done, keeping track of the little details that nobody else wants to keep track of. I’ve done it enough years that people sort of expect me to be steady with it. But since the robbery, I just haven’t been keeping up with it the way I usually would. I’ll look at a list or think, “I should call so-and-so,” and then I put it aside. And then the day goes by. It makes me feel bad, because it’s important to me and to other people too.

And with friends… I’ve stopped going to card nights. That’s something I usually enjoy. It’s not even a big serious thing, just sitting around, talking, playing cards, seeing familiar faces. But right now I don’t feel very steady around people. I don’t quite know how to explain it — I just feel like I can’t relax and be myself there, so I’ve been staying away.

So yes, I guess it has affected things. Not in a dramatic fight-with-family kind of way, but I’m pulling back from the usual things and the usual people more than I’d like.
Have you experienced any significant reduction in your symptoms over the past week?

I don’t think I could honestly say there’s been a significant reduction, no. I wish I could say that, because I keep sort of checking myself day by day, thinking, “Well, maybe today feels a little easier,” but then I’m not sure if that’s really improvement or just that I got through that particular day.

Over the past week, it’s felt more like… uneven, I guess. Some parts of a day might feel a little quieter, and then later I realize I’m still not back to how I was. So I wouldn’t call it a big change for the better. If anything, it feels like I’m still in the middle of it and trying to figure out whether it’s easing up at all.

So, no, not a significant reduction that I’ve noticed.

I’ll tell myself the other route is fine, that it only adds a little time, that I needed the walk anyway… but underneath that, I know I’m doing it because I don’t want to see the bank. Even just being near it makes the whole thing feel too close again, like I’m right back at that feeling.

And the festival storage room is similar. I haven’t gone in there because it’s tied to all of it now in my head. I keep thinking I should just open the door and get on with what needs doing, but then I stop myself. So, no, I don’t think it’s just a preference. It feels like I’m avoiding those places because it’s the only way I can keep myself from getting stirred up.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of the patient's avoidance behaviors
doctor.question: Would you say that avoiding these places or activities is significantly impacting your ability to function in your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I haven't been able to keep up with organizing the Día de los Muertos event the way I usually do, and I've stopped going to card nights because I don't feel steady around people right now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the avoidance is significantly affecting daily functioning, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yes… I’d say it is, though maybe not in a way where everything has fallen apart. I’m still getting through the day, but I’m not functioning like I normally do.

The clearest thing is the Día de los Muertos event. I usually help organize things, and people kind of count on me to keep track of what needs to be done. I’ve done that for years, so it bothers me that I haven’t been keeping up with it the way I usually would. I’ll mean to make a call, or check on something, or go handle something, and then I just… don’t. Or I put it off because it means being around certain places or people, and then I feel bad because someone else has to pick up the slack.

And I’ve stopped going to card nights too, which is a regular part of my week. That may sound small, but at my age those routines matter. It’s where I see people, talk, laugh a little, feel normal. Lately I don’t feel steady enough around people, like I’d have to pretend I’m fine the whole time, and I just don’t have it in me. So I stay home instead.

So yes, it’s affecting my daily life. Mildly maybe, compared to some people, but enough that I notice I’m pulling back from the things I normally do.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of the patient's avoidance behaviors
doctor.question: Would you say that avoiding these places or activities is something you feel like you're doing most of the time, or is it more occasional?

target_item.name: Trauma_Avoidance
target_item.manifestation: I've been taking the long way around so I don't pass the bank, and I haven't gone into the festival storage room because it brings the whole thing too close.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how often the patient avoids places or activities connected to the traumatic event, which directly corresponds to trauma-related avoidance.

patient.answer:
I’d say it’s more than occasional, yes. Not every single minute of the day, but it’s become sort of… built into how I’m moving around now.

Like with the bank, I’ve been taking the long way around so I don’t have to pass it. At first I told myself it was just once or twice, just because I didn’t feel up to it that day. But then I noticed I was doing it again, and again, almost without even deciding. I’ll be walking or driving and before I know it, I’ve already planned a route that keeps me away from there. It’s not like I sit down and make a big dramatic decision about it — it’s more automatic than that. I just don’t want to see it, don’t want to get that feeling in my chest, so I go around.

And with the festival storage room, I haven’t gone in there at all. I know there are probably things in there I should be checking on, and normally I would’ve just gone in, looked over the supplies, made a list, done what needed doing. But now even thinking about opening that door makes the whole thing feel too close again. So I keep putting it off.

So… I guess I’d say it’s happening most of the time when those places come up. It’s not that I’m avoiding everything in life, but those specific places, yes — I keep steering away from them.

doctor.question: Have your symptoms been present for more than a month?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a week, ever since the robbery outside the bank.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the symptoms have been present, which directly corresponds to the duration item.

patient.answer:
No… no, it hasn’t been more than a month. It feels longer, honestly, because the days have been sort of dragging, but when I count it out, it’s only been about a week.

It started after the robbery outside the bank. Ever since then, that’s when all of this really began. So, no — not a month. More like a week, maybe a little over or under depending on how you count it, but about a week.

doctor.intent: Determine the duration of symptoms to differentiate between acute stress disorder and other conditions
doctor.question: Have your symptoms been getting worse or staying about the same since they started?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the course or progression of symptoms over time—whether they are worsening or staying the same—which is not specifically covered by any listed symptom profile item.

patient.answer:
I’m not completely sure how to judge that, to be honest. It hasn’t been that long, so part of me feels like I don’t have enough distance from it yet to say, “Oh, this is clearly worse,” or “this is clearly better.”

Some moments feel about the same as they did right after it started, and then other moments catch me off guard and feel heavier. But I don’t know if that means it’s actually getting worse, or if I’m just more tired from dealing with it day after day. You know, after a few days of being on edge and rearranging what I do, it sort of wears you down, so it can feel worse even if the actual problem hasn’t changed much.

If I had to put it simply, I’d say it’s mostly staying about the same… maybe with some ups and downs. I haven’t noticed a clear steady improvement, but I also don’t think I can honestly say it’s been sharply getting worse. It’s just still there, and I’m still having to work around it.

doctor.intent: determine if symptoms are significantly impacting social relationships
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since the robbery?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I haven't been able to keep up with organizing the Día de los Muertos event the way I usually do, and I've stopped going to card nights because I don't feel steady around people right now.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about social and relationship changes since the robbery, which is most directly covered by the functional impairment profile, including stopping card nights and difficulty keeping up with usual community activities.

patient.answer:
Yes… I have noticed some changes. I wouldn’t say I’ve cut everybody off or anything like that, but I’m not showing up the way I usually do.

The biggest thing is the Día de los Muertos event. Normally I’m pretty involved with organizing it — making calls, checking what still needs to be done, keeping track of the little details that nobody else wants to keep track of. I’ve done it enough years that people sort of expect me to be steady with it. But since the robbery, I just haven’t been keeping up with it the way I usually would. I’ll look at a list or think, “I should call so-and-so,” and then I put it aside. And then the day goes by. It makes me feel bad, because it’s important to me and to other people too.

And with friends… I’ve stopped going to card nights. That’s something I usually enjoy. It’s not even a big serious thing, just sitting around, talking, playing cards, seeing familiar faces. But right now I don’t feel very steady around people. I don’t quite know how to explain it — I just feel like I can’t relax and be myself there, so I’ve been staying away.

So yes, I guess it has affected things. Not in a dramatic fight-with-family kind of way, but I’m pulling back from the usual things and the usual people more than I’d like.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the duration criteria for the diagnosis
doctor.question: Have you experienced any significant reduction in your symptoms over the past week?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether symptoms have significantly reduced over the past week, which is a change/improvement over time. The provided symptom profile includes duration but does not include symptom reduction or improvement as an item.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I could honestly say there’s been a significant reduction, no. I wish I could say that, because I keep sort of checking myself day by day, thinking, “Well, maybe today feels a little easier,” but then I’m not sure if that’s really improvement or just that I got through that particular day.

Over the past week, it’s felt more like… uneven, I guess. Some parts of a day might feel a little quieter, and then later I realize I’m still not back to how I was. So I wouldn’t call it a big change for the better. If anything, it feels like I’m still in the middle of it and trying to figure out whether it’s easing up at all.

So, no, not a significant reduction that I’ve noticed.
